summary.claim: Over-refusal directions are task-dependent and high-dimensional, while harmful-refusal is a single task-agnostic direction. Ablating the global refusal direction reduces over-refusal only by accident and breaks the refusal mechanism, so task-specific geometric interventions are needed.
summary.condition: Geometry analysis and linear probing of hidden states in aligned language models; the two refusal types separate from early layers.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The abstract names no models or datasets, and it is unclear whether a task-specific intervention was built and tested.
